compliance_rules: NMLS license required — display on all advertising and communications
Equal Housing Lender disclosure required on all marketing materials
RESPA prohibits kickbacks and referral fees
TILA requires full APR disclosure on any rate advertising
TRID requires loan estimate within 3 business days of application
State-specific licensing required in each state where loans are originated
Regulation Z governs advertising of credit terms
customer_journey: awareness: buyer begins researching home purchase or refinance options
consideration: buyer compares loan officers, rates, and lender reviews
pre-approval: loan officer collects documents and issues pre-approval letter
processing: underwriting, appraisal, title search, and final approval
closing: signing, funding, and key handoff
ranking_factors: Google Business Profile with NMLS number in description
review volume and recency on GBP and Zillow Mortgage
hyper-local content targeting specific city and neighborhood markets
schema markup with Person type, hasCredential, and areaServed
citations in mortgage-specific directories and real estate platforms
expertise_signals: NMLS license — verified on Consumer Access
FHA and VA approved lender status
closed loan volume in specific markets

ai_agents.review_response_style: Warm and personal — reference the specific transaction type and thank by name
ai_agents.compliance_restrictions: Never mention specific rates without full APR disclosure. Never guarantee approval. Always include NMLS ID in any regulated communication.

required_disclaimers: NMLS # [number] displayed on all advertising, websites, and business cards per SAFE Act
Equal Housing Lender or Equal Housing Opportunity logo required on all marketing materials
Rates and terms subject to change without notice; not a commitment to lend
Not all applicants will qualify; approval subject to underwriting
This is not a commitment to make a mortgage loan; subject to property appraisal and title
Reverse mortgage: borrowers must be 62+, maintain property, pay taxes and insurance; loan becomes due on sale or vacancy
APR and payment examples must reflect actual costs per Regulation Z / TRID
State licensing disclosure required in all states where originating loans
Affiliated business arrangement disclosure required under RESPA Section 8 where applicable
HMDA data collected and reported annually as required by federal law
content_restrictions: All rate and payment advertising must comply with Regulation Z (Truth in Lending Act) triggering terms
UDAP (Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices) prohibition under CFPB authority
RESPA Section 8 prohibits kickbacks or unearned fees in settlement service referral arrangements
CAN-SPAM and TCPA compliance required for email and SMS marketing
Fair Housing Act prohibits steering or discriminatory marketing targeting
State-specific mortgage advertising disclosure laws may impose additional labeling requirements
Social media advertising must include NMLS ID and Equal Housing Lender disclosure
Testimonials and endorsements must comply with FTC Endorsement Guides (16 CFR Part 255)
prohibited_phrases: we will match any rate guaranteed
rates as low as [X]% for all borrowers
regulated_by: State Department of Financial Institutions / Division of Banking (jurisdiction-specific)
U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) — for FHA and HECM
U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) — for VA loan approval
USDA Rural Development — for USDA loan approval
Federal Trade Commission (FTC) — advertising and unfair practices
